project.description: The project: an absolute path inside it (default: this session's project).

checkout.description: create/up: an existing worktree (absolute path) to run as an instance.

branch.description: create/up: a branch; Sova adds a worktree for it (new branches start at `from`). merge.try: the branch whose head to trial (default your own).

from.description: create/up with a new branch: the commit it starts at (default the main checkout's HEAD).

restart.description: apply: restart instead of each service's reload.

ref.description: conform: the branch or commit whose definition to prove (default the main checkout's HEAD).

endpoint.description: share/revoke: the endpoint, "<service>.<port>", one of the definition's share.endpoints.

days.description: share: how many days the link lasts (default 1, at most 7 or the definition's share.maxDays).

link.description: revoke: one share link, by its id (pv_…).

target.description: deploy.*: the deploy target, by name (deploy.status lists them).

commit.description: deploy.plan/deploy.request: the commit to ship (default the target branch's tip); merge.try: the commit to trial.

plan.description: deploy.run: a plan's id (pl_…); only the operator runs one.

deploy.description: deploy.logs: one deploy, by its id (dp_…; default the target's latest).

why.description: deploy.request (and onboard): why, one line for the operator.

release.description: release.*: a release, by its id (rl_…; default the open one).

state.description: release.step: running | done | failed | skipped | held.

summary.description: release.step: the step's result in one line (at most 300 characters).

detail.description: release.step: what the step did, in full (optional).

facts.description: release.step: facts Sova checks, each key=value: version, commit, branch, url, artifact (a path), sha256, size.

tag.description: release.withdraw: the published release, by its numbered tag (instead of its id).

entry.description: merge.*: a queue entry, by its id (mq_…; merge.status lists them).

run.description: merge.logs/merge.review: a run, by its id (mr_…).

step.description: merge.logs: one step of the run, by its id (default every step's tail).

note.description: merge.note (and every merge verb the merge thread calls): the entry's note, short free text shown on its row (at most 300 characters; empty clears it).

checks.description: merge.extend {entry, checks, why, select}: check ids from the project's merge section to add to this entry's run (never removes one); send each pick's select with it; merge.try: release check ids to run although unchanged.

verdict.description: merge.resolve: no-behaviour-change (your resolution commit) | chat-fixes (the branch's chat fixes it; your diagnosis in proposal) | needs-user (the user decides; question in text, choices); merge.review: ok | notes | blocking.

files.description: merge.resolve: the conflicted files the judgement covers.

ours.description: merge.resolve: what the target's side does, in plain words.

theirs.description: merge.resolve: what the branch's side does, in plain words.

proposal.description: merge.resolve: what the resolution does, in plain words.

answer.description: merge.respond (the branch's chat, answering a merge queue request by its id): fixed | needs-you | cant.

request.description: merge.respond / merge.rule: a merge queue request, by its id (rq_…, in the merge queue's note).

drafts.description: merge.respond with fixed: you changed the branch's spec drafts (that needs no commit).

choices.description: merge.rule / merge.resolve with needs-user, merge.respond with needs-you: the options for the user, short, at most 4 (each fills the chat's message box when picked).

action.description: merge.hold (the merge thread's): set | clear. set holds every new run for 5 minutes (set again renews it); a run already checking goes on.

ask.description: merge.reply (the user's page only): the merge thread's question the user answers, by its id (ak_…).
